zh.title: 英國皇家空軍Hawk T2教練機威爾斯墜毀 兩飛行員彈射受輕傷
zh.summary: Hawk T2墜毀安格爾西島；兩飛行員彈射獲救；傷勢輕微；展開調查
body: 英國皇家空軍一架Hawk T2高級教練機於9月23日下午在威爾斯北部安格爾西島RAF Valley（RAF）附近墜毀。兩名飛行員成功彈射逃生，警方表示傷勢被認為輕微。
皇家空軍發言人證實，事故涉及一架從RAF Valley起飛的T2 Hawk飛機，事故發生在安格爾西島附近。調查已經啟動，目前不再進一步置評。北威爾斯警方表示，警員正在應對安格爾西島Pencarnisiog地區涉及皇家空軍訓練飛機的事件。
皇家空軍、北威爾斯消防救援局、威爾斯救護服務和Helimed空中救護直升機均已趕赴現場。消防部門稍後表示墜機現場火勢已受控，呼籲民眾避開該區域。皇家空軍指出兩名飛行員在彈射後不久即被尋獲。
據報導，RAF Valley是第4飛行訓練學校所在地，該校使用Hawk T2培訓預備駕駛Typhoon和F-35B的飛行員。事故前該校運營28架Hawk T2機隊，長期面臨可用性問題。2023年1月，因跑道發動機問題曾暫停Hawk T2飛行，疑與勞斯萊斯Turbomeca Adour Mk 951發動機葉片磨損有關。
英國國防部正尋找Hawk繼任機型。2025年戰略防務評審要求以更具成本效益的高性能教練機取代Hawk T1和T2。2026年8月7日，國防部發布新型高性能教練機的資訊請求，涵蓋訓練機隊和紅箭特技飛行隊，國防投資計劃撥資3.6億英鎊（約4.85億美元），回應窗口於9月11日關閉。

en.title: RAF Hawk T2 trainer crashes in Wales, both pilots eject with minor injuries
en.summary: Hawk T2 crashes in Anglesey; both pilots eject safely; minor injuries; investigation launched
body: A Royal Air Force Hawk T2 advanced jet trainer crashed near RAF Valley (RAF) on the island of Anglesey, North Wales, on the afternoon of September 23, 2026. Both pilots ejected and were located shortly afterwards. Police said their injuries were thought to be minor.

An RAF spokesperson confirmed an incident involving an RAF T2 Hawk aircraft flying out of RAF Valley occurred near Anglesey, adding that an investigation is underway and the service would not comment further at this time. North Wales Police said officers were responding to an incident involving an RAF training aircraft in the Pencarnisiog area of Anglesey.

The RAF, North Wales Fire and Rescue Service, the Welsh Ambulance Service and the Helimed air ambulance were all at the scene. The fire service later reported the fire at the crash site was under control and asked the public to avoid the area.

RAF Valley hosts No. 4 Flying Training School, which uses the Hawk T2 to prepare pilots for the Typhoon and F-35B. Before the crash, the school operated a fleet of 28 Hawk T2 aircraft that has had persistent availability problems. In January 2023, the RAF temporarily paused Hawk T2 flying after an engine issue on the runway at RAF Valley, reportedly linked to blade wear on the Rolls-Royce Turbomeca Adour Mk 951 engine.

The loss comes as the UK Ministry of Defence seeks a successor to the Hawk. The 2025 Strategic Defence Review called for the Hawk T1 and T2 to be replaced by a more cost-effective fast jet trainer. On August 7, 2026, the ministry published a request for information for a new advanced jet trainer covering both the training fleet and the Red Arrows, with £360 million ($485 million) allocated in the Defence Investment Plan. The response window closed on September 11, 2026.
